exam_name: LFCS Linux Foundation Certified Systems Administrator
aliases: LFCS Linux Foundation Certified Systems Administrator

editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the Linux Foundation Certified Systems Administrator certification covering 5 domains of sysadmin skills across a 120-minute exam.
editorial.overview: The LFCS Linux Foundation Certified Systems Administrator examination is administered directly by the Linux Foundation. It measures practical technical competency across five distinct domains, including operations deployment, networking configurations, storage management, essential commands, and user administration. Candidates must successfully complete this assessment within a strict time limit of 120 minutes, directly demonstrating hands-on command-line abilities in a simulated environment.
editorial.who_should_take: Junior to mid-level Linux system administrators and IT professionals seeking to validate their practical operational capabilities. Candidates should have hands-on experience managing system services, users, and storage volumes in production environments.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Practice configuring system services directly on a terminal to build strong operational habits. Focus heavily on managing systemd units, setting up complex network parameters, and handling file storage volumes without relying on any graphical user interface tools. Review all commands referenced in the official exam guide and third-party documentation extensively before test day arrives to ensure maximum efficiency.

domain_guidance.summary: This specific domain comprehensively covers operations deployment topics, representing exactly 25.0 percent of the complete evaluation, focusing primarily on managing system services, startup configurations, and initialization parameters.

Focuses intently on important networking tasks with a 25.0 percent weight, testing interface configuration, connectivity troubleshooting, name resolution mechanisms, and essential network services for standard enterprise environments effectively.

Allocated 20.0 percent of the total exam weight, this specific domain requires managing advanced storage devices, complex file systems, persistent mount options, and underlying volume structures reliably.

Comprises exactly 20.0 percent of the entire test evaluation, concentrating deeply on essential commands, text processing utilities, and core operating system tools used daily in standard Linux administration.

Accounts for precisely 10.0 percent of the certification exam, carefully validating the secure creation and administration of user accounts, administrative groups, file permission structures, and access attributes.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Ensure your testing environment meets all official proctoring requirements. Manage your 120-minute time limit carefully across the tasks. Read each prompt completely before executing commands on the terminal.

faq.question_title: How many domains are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The certification exam features 5 distinct domains, systematically covering operations deployment, networking, storage, essential commands, and users and groups, with evaluation weights distributed carefully across them.
The exam has a strict duration of 120 minutes. Candidates must complete all practical technical tasks within this designated timeframe to achieve a passing score.

This professional certification is officially administered, governed, and awarded directly by the Linux Foundation to verify real-world hands-on systems administration skills for modern enterprise environments.

faq.question_title: What is the long-term certification path?
faq.answer_text: This exam is currently active. For any future credential path updates or program changes, check directly with the Linux Foundation for the current certification path.
